claims.claim: Serve's causal chain runs from autonomous sidewalk robotics through fleet availability and merchant/platform integration to lower-cost last-mile delivery; expanded platform relationships widen demand access but utilization is the successor bottleneck.
The Uber Eats volume shortfall demonstrates that deployed fleet scale is not sufficient: delivery density and partner demand must convert physical capacity into economically productive utilization.

risks.risk: Human couriers, e-bikes, drones and other autonomous systems remain substitutes; local density and operating-domain constraints can shift the bottleneck from autonomy to utilization.

contradictions.contradiction: Operational footprint and partner count expanded while 2026 revenue expectations materially declined.

unknowns.unknown: Platform-level unit economics and utilization are not fully disclosed.

claims.claim: The 2026 guidance cut tied to lower-than-expected Uber Eats volume is direct falsification pressure against any thesis that fleet expansion alone guarantees revenue conversion.
Partner diversification through Grubhub improves resilience but does not yet resolve the observed demand-utilization contradiction.

risks.risk: Absolute revenue remains small, increasing financing sensitivity while the network is scaled.
Demand concentration and platform bargaining power can impair utilization and pricing even if robot technology performs.

contradictions.contradiction: Rapid platform expansion contrasts with lower-than-expected Uber Eats delivery volume that caused a full-year guidance cut.

unknowns.unknown: Whether newer partners can offset removed demand within the next reporting periods is unknown.
